edits.old:
There are two choices of matrices. The universal matrix consists of
the six rows
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-p0rows}
 R_{ab},R_{bs},R_{as},T_{ab},T_{bs},T_{sa}.
\end{equation}
In columns $(Q_0,Q_a,Q_b,Q_s)$, the determinant of its first three
rows and $T_{ab}$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-p0det}
 15750a^2b^2s^2(a-b)^4(a-s)(b-s)F_s,
 \quad F_s=7(2s-a-b)+6c[3s^2-(a+b)s-ab].
\end{equation}
The alternative four-row matrix is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-prows}
 R_{ab},\quad H=R_{ab}+R_{bs}-R_{as},\quad
 T_{ab},\quad V=T_{as}-T_{bs};
\end{equation}
its determinant is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-pdet}
 -78750a^2b^2s^2(a-b)^5(a-s)(b-s)F_s.
\end{equation}
Both identities are checked from the printed rows by expanding only
the constant and linear coefficients in $c$. Replacement of the column indexed by $0$ by its $O(c^{-5})$ residual makes their determinant degree at
most $2+2+2-5=1$. Thus this finite expansion verifies the complete
identities, with no unspecified higher coefficients.

The universal matrix always has rank four. Its cyclic minors have
the nonzero products displayed in \eqref{eq:ff-p0det}
times $F_a,F_b,F_s$, up to signs. With
$\sigma_1=a+b+s$, $\sigma_2=ab+as+bs$, these factors are
\[
 F_x=7(3x-\sigma_1)+6c(3x^2-\sigma_2).
\]
If all three vanished, subtracting the equations for $s,b$ and $s,a$
would give $7+6c(s+b)=7+6c(s+a)=0$, contrary to $c\ne0$ and $a\ne b$.
For the four-row matrix it suffices to prove $F_s\ne0$.
If $S\ge2B$, then
\[
 |3s^2-(a+b)s-ab|\ge\tfrac74S^2,\qquad |2s-a-b|\le3S,
\]
so the $c$ term dominates under \eqref{eq:ff-pguards}.
Alternatively, if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-allSrank}
 B\ge qA,\qquad q\ge18/17,\qquad S\ge3,
\end{equation}
then for every $S\ge B$,
\[
 |3s^2-(a+b)s-ab|\ge(2-2/q)S^2,
 \qquad |2s-a-b|\le(3+1/q)S.
\]
Indeed $6C(2-2/q)S^2\ge1200(2-2/q)S^3$
is strictly larger than $7(3+1/q)S$ already at $q=18/17$, $S=3$.
Thus the matrix has rank four under these hypotheses.
edits.replacement:
Use the four rows
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-prows}
 R_{ab},\quad H=R_{ab}+R_{bs}-R_{as},\quad
 T_{ab},\quad V=T_{as}-T_{bs}.
\end{equation}
In columns $(Q_0,Q_a,Q_b,Q_s)$, their determinant is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-pdet}
 -78750a^2b^2s^2(a-b)^5(a-s)(b-s)F_s,
\end{equation}
where
\[
 F_s=7(2s-a-b)+6c[3s^2-(a+b)s-ab].
\]
Replacing column zero by its $O(c^{-5})$ residual shows that the
polynomial determinant has degree at most $2+2+2-5=1$ in $c$.
Expanding its constant and linear coefficients from the displayed rows
gives the identity.

Suppose that $F_s=0$. If $3s^2-(a+b)s-ab\ne0$, this algebraic integer
has modulus at least one, and
\[
 6C\le7|2s-a-b|\le28S,
\]
contrary to $C\ge200S$. Otherwise $a+b=2s$ and $ab=s^2$, so
$a=b=s$, again a contradiction. Thus the matrix has rank four.
edits.reason: Prove unconditional rank by integrality and remove the unnecessary six-row alternative.

Thus $23/10$ is a valid residual constant without a ratio restriction

For the complementary range $S<2B$, use the universal matrix
\eqref{eq:ff-p0rows} and put
$H_0=\max(S^4,B^5)$, $J_0=\max(S,B^2)$.
The degree sums of its $R$ rows are $(84,408,384)$ and those of its
$T$ rows are $(252,1224,1200)$. Their anchor monomials are at most
$S^4\le H_0$ and $S^5<32B^5\le32H_0$, respectively. Hence their
approximation coefficient is less than
\[
 \frac{101}{100}\max\left(384+\frac{408}{1000}+\frac{84}{10^6},
 32\left(1200+\frac{1224}{1000}+\frac{252}{10^6}\right)\right)
 <39000.
\]
The first residual monomials in an $R$ row are bounded by $S/A^3$,
and in a $T$ row by $S^2/A^3$. From \eqref{eq:ff-leading}, their
leading absolute coefficient sums are $15/128$ and $25/16$; their
original integer coefficient sums are $876$ and $2676$.
Using $S\le J_0$ and $S^2<4J_0$ gives the residual coefficient
\[
 \max\left(\frac{15}{128}+\tau\,876,
       4\left(\frac{25}{16}+\tau\,2676\right)\right)
 =\frac{45961}{7104}<\frac{13}{2}.
\]
Thus, throughout $S<2B$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ff-P0}
 1<\frac{39000H_0C^3}{Z}+\frac{13J_0Z}{2A^3C^5}.
\end{equation}
When $B\ge3$, $S<2B\le B^2$ implies $J_0=B^2$.
Equations \eqref{eq:ff-P} and \eqref{eq:ff-P0}, together with
\eqref{eq:ff-window}, specify their closed forbidden intervals.
